chapter: On the road, James Brown and the 1956 crash
title: Ben Barth stood by him; why he carries heavy insurance
summary: Cobb says Ben Barth stayed in his corner and he never borrowed from him, helped by insurance that he still carries heavily.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Was that for Universal? And that

I stayed with Ben all the way. Ben was in my corner all the way. He didn't know if I was going to come back, but he still stuck with me and still sold the told (inaudible), I got money over here. If you ever need anything. -- I never got in debt. I never borrowed $100.00 from him. I took care of myself. I mean after the accident too.
That was largely due to the, you know, the fact that you got that good insurance.

(Inaudible) my insurance (inaudible). Well, you see, like I told you, I was insurance conscious, and if anything happened, I didn't want to put any strain on my wife, me laying up -- and (inaudible) end up -- I could have if I wasn't wise enough to get it, but I'm insurance conscious today. I've got more insurance than I can really pay for, but I'm going to pay for it because I don't want nobody to suffer (inaudible) behind me, and I'm [subject to] go in the hospital any day, you know.
